facts: A **cluster** is a group of data values grouped closely around each other.
A dataset can contain more than one cluster.
A **gap** is an interval that contains no data values.
Describe a gap by naming the two values it lies between.
An **outlier** is a data value **much higher or much lower** than all the others, so it stands alone.
Ordering the data first makes every cluster, gap and outlier easy to see.
steps: Order the data values from smallest to largest
Identify any value far from all the others (an outlier)
Identify any interval with no data values (a gap)
Identify any group of values bunched closely together (a cluster)

workedExamples.question_text:
The heights, in metres, of six trees are $7.4$, $6.8$, $7.1$, $7.6$, $18.9$ and $7.2$.
Describe the cluster, the gap and the outlier.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Order the heights: $6.8,7.1,7.2,7.4,7.6,18.9$.
Five heights are close together from $6.8$ m to $7.6$ m, so this is the cluster.
There is a gap between $7.6$ m and $18.9$ m: no tree has a recorded height in that interval.
The outlier is $18.9$ m, much higher than the other five trees.

(a) Read the temperature scale, not the day numbers: $14,16,15,31,17,16$ in day order.
(b) In order: $14,15,16,16,17,31$.
Five temperatures are close together from $14^{\circ}$C to $17^{\circ}$C, forming a cluster.
There is a gap between $17^{\circ}$C and $31^{\circ}$C, with no recorded temperature in that interval.
The outlier is $31^{\circ}$C on Day $4$, much higher than the other five temperatures.

(a) Plot B has ten heights from $11$ m to $13$ m and three heights at $21$ m. These form two groups.
There is a gap between $13$ m and $21$ m, with no heights at the ticks $14$ m to $20$ m.
(b) Plot A has a single outlier at $21$ m, far above the group from $11$ m to $13$ m.
In Plot B, three trees have height $21$ m. They form a second group, rather than a single height standing alone.

workedExamples.question_text:
Two streets have these house prices, in thousands of dollars:
Street A: $\$43,\$56,\$69,\$82,\$95,\$108$
Street B: $\$43,\$46,\$48,\$51,\$54,\$108$
Both have the same lowest and highest prices. Which street has an outlier? Explain why the highest price is not automatically an outlier.
workedExamples.solution_text:
In Street A the prices rise in equal steps of $\$13$ thousand. No price sits far from the rest, so there is no outlier.
In Street B, five prices are grouped from $\$43$ thousand to $\$54$ thousand. The price $\$108$ thousand is much higher and stands alone, so it is an outlier.
Both streets have the same spread, but only Street B has an isolated price. The highest price is an outlier only when it is far from the rest.

workedExamples.question_text: Which value is the outlier in $\frac{3}{5},\frac{31}{50},\frac{3}{20},0.57,\frac{29}{50},\frac{59}{100}$?
workedExamples.solution_text:
Write the fractions as decimals: $0.60,0.62,0.15,0.57,0.58,0.59$.
In order: $0.15,0.57,0.58,0.59,0.60,0.62$.
Five values cluster from $0.57$ to $0.62$. The outlier is $\frac{3}{20}=0.15$, much lower than the other five values.

Use the key to read the values: $32,35,38,41,43,46,67,68,69,70,72$.
Six values cluster from $32$ to $46$, and five values cluster from $67$ to $72$.
The large gap is between $46$ and $67$, with no data values in that interval. The empty stem $5$ shows that there are no values from $50$ to $59$.

foundation.question_text:
The heights, in metres, of six trees in a park are $4.2$, $3.8$, $4.5$, $12.6$, $4.0$ and $3.9$.
Which height is the outlier?
foundation.solution_text:
$3.8, 3.9, 4.0, 4.2, 4.5, 12.6$
The outlier is $12.6$ m, because it is much higher than every other height.

The outlier is $12^{\circ}$C, because it is much lower than every other temperature.

development.question_text:
The heights, in metres, of six trees in a park are $1.2$, $7.8$, $8.1$, $8.4$, $8.6$ and $9.0$.
Which height is the outlier?
development.solution_text:
$1.2, 7.8, 8.1, 8.4, 8.6, 9.0$
The outlier is $1.2$ m, because it is much lower than every other height.
The largest height, $9.0$ m, is only $0.4$ m above the next one, so it is not an outlier.

In order: $0.30, 0.87, 0.88, 0.89, 0.90, 0.92$.
The outlier is $\frac{3}{10}=0.30$, because it is much lower than the other five values.
